title: Finalize, ship and archive refuse an approvals ledger that Git history does not hold
description: finalize, ship and archive refuse an approvals ledger that Git history does not hold
acceptance_criteria: `change finalize`, `change ship` and `change archive` refuse, writing nothing, a change whose `approvals.json` is not committed at `HEAD` or differs from the committed version, naming the file and the way out: the commit when the working copy only adds records, the restore when it changes a committed one.

They refuse when a committed version of the ledger rewrites or drops an earlier approval, reopening or send-back, naming the commit that did it, the commit before it and the record; that covers a change deleted and created again under the same id, and a record an older SpecSync rewrote without a member it did not know.

Every rewrite the tool itself makes still finalizes: a reopen, a send-back and fresh approval, a relay restored or removed by `change repair-relays` in an approval or in the approval a reopening embeds, the reopening members `specsync migrate 5.0` backfills, and a ledger member this version does not know.
An accepted change archives with the closing records its accepting step wrote and has not committed, and no other uncommitted approval.
`change ship-status` lists the refusal as a blocker and does not report the change ready, and `change ship --dry-run` refuses with it.
The usual flow, approve, `check --commit`, review and finalize, archives as before.

answers.constraints: CHANGE-16 to CHANGE-16.c and Leif's choice 'Every committed version' (2026-11-13); REQ-change-relay-repair-001: repair-relays restores or removes relays, so relayed_by is not compared, in an approval and in a reopening's embedded approval; the change lesson that one rule kept in two places drifts, so the comparison reuses the #660 relay-blind projection; the change lesson that a printed recovery command must run as printed, so each way out is a command that does what the refusal says; #1044: lifecycle rewrites keep members they do not know, so a newer top-level member is not a rewrite
